Article Title: Meet Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school student appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador
Article Text: Born in Japan, and raised in Nepal during her early childhood, Aditi Paudel had always shown an affinity towards reading. Her earliest memory of reading is of her grandfather handing her a newspaper filled with intricate Devanagari script when she was still in preschool. But to the surprise of those around her, she was still able to make sense of the text. Over the years, she has only improved and the now 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador, as per a report by The Japan Times.The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. While the program has been running for 12 years, this is the first time an ambassador from Japan has been appointed, according to Andrew Kay, CEO and founder of the World Literacy Foundation.The aim of the program is to connect young people around the world and get them “involved and waving the flag for literacy in their community,” Kay said, noting that Paudel was singled out “for her leadership, passion for literacy, and commitment to empowering young people in Japan.”“Her curiosity about English shaped thoughtful advocacy, strengthening the program’s global voice and cultural reach,” he added.Paudel returned to Japan to enter the third grade and along with settling into a new life, she found herself having to learn Japanese once more, which meant turning to the books. Her love for reading came pretty early in her life, nurtured by her father who bought her plenty of books. She developed an early taste for fantasy, and recalled falling in love with Enid Blyton’s “The Wishing-Chair.”Reading Malala Yousafzai 's autobiography, 'I Am Malala', helped her develop significant interests in female empowerment, including ensuring that women across the world have access to education and literacy. Along with working with children with disabilities, she plans to work with the Shanti Volunteer Association to collect and donate books to Asian countries with lower rates of literacy, including Nepal.With enough experience developing her own reading skills, Paudel said that a common view of literacy is how well a person can read or write, but she sees it in broader terms. Essentially, it’s “something that helps you open doors for more opportunities,” she noted.Paudel has experienced the impact of her access to private education firsthand and how it has set her life on a different course. “My parents grew up in a completely opposite environment. They did not have a childhood like this,” she said. “Being literate is so important because even though you have the potential, you can never unlock it if you do not have literacy.”But even those with easy access to books are reading less than they once did. Around half of elementary, junior high and high school age children in Japan do not read books, according to a recent study by Benesse Educational Research & Development Institute and the University of Tokyo.Fewer young people are reading for pleasure and enjoyment, said Kay, and that could cause a significant regressive effect. “As far as embedding themselves in a novel or reading something that really takes a little bit more effort, that is becoming a rarer thing,” he said. Kay also cautions against the impact of artificial intelligence, noting that the latest tech tools provide quick answers, allowing people to skip the process of researching, reading and wrestling with theories and thoughts oneself.“It’s turning our clock back 150 years … where most people couldn’t read or would have limited ability to read,” he said of the absence of reading books as a mainstream pursuit. Those trends only add importance to initiatives like the World Literacy Foundation’s ambassador program.As a teenager, Paudel understands what it is like to grow up surrounded by distractions, with much of life centred around social media. “You will always be more inclined to go for your phone rather than a book,” she said. That is why she believes building a reading habit is important. Her advice is not to work through a list of classic books, but to find something that connects with you. Ideally, she said, reading should also help broaden your perspective.
Article Summary: Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo, was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador. The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating.

Article Title: Barefoot mom in sari runs 3km to win Rs 5k for kids' education
Article Text:
Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Ramabai Ranvir had no idea what running a race meant. All she had heard was there was Rs 3,000 to be won if she finished first.So, the 47-year-old widow hopped onto the pickup with a group of police aspirants from the Beed academy where she worked, hoping to compete in what would be the first race of her life. It didn't bother her that she hadn't trained for the rigours of a long-distance run. It hardly mattered that she was the lone runner without shoes.In her sari, barefoot after her slippers gave up midway through the run, Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize that would ease her struggle to pay for her daughters' education."I ran like my life depended on it. I didn't know how much time I needed to cover the distance. I only sto-pped once I was past the finish line," she told TOI. "I am so happy they gave me Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 3,000. I bought notebooks and pens for my daughter Pooja. The remaining money is for Arti."Ramabai works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.The native of Potra, Hingoli, took the job to fund the education of her two daughters after her husband died in 2012.On Aug 28, her younger daughter Arti (20), a BSc computer science student who lives alone in Nanded, called asking for money for food and rent. Ramabai, who didn't have any cash to spare, had a sleepless night.At dawn, she heard the academy's trainers rounding up aspirants for a running competition nearby. She instantly decided to join in."There is no pain worse than that of not being able to take care of your children. The moment I came to know of the race, winning was the only thing on my mind."Datta Darade, who heads the academy, said Ramabai's determination moved him. The academy had enrolled her elder daughter Pooja (22) free of cost and given her employment and a room to stay in. "I was taking my students to the marathon. When Ramabai said she wanted to come along, I asked her, 'What will you do there?' She said, 'I will run.' I couldn't believe it when she won in the above-30 category."Pooja finished second in the 18-30 age group and won Rs 2,000. Arti said she was dumbstruck when her sister called to say their mother had won."Our mother studied till Class 7 and has worked all her life, not taking breaks even when she was unwell. She didn't hesitate to send me to Nanded for my studies. I am not surprised she decided to win a race for her family," she said.
Article Summary: Ramabai Ranvir ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize. The 47-year-old widow works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.

Article Title: Tribunal alters gay ex-IAF man 'dismissal' to 'routine discharge'
Article Text:
Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to being gay, into a routine discharge.The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces.The non-commissioned IAF officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry. The inquiry concluded he had breached discipline and risked national security by entering into a relationship with a foreigner. The court of inquiry also found him guilty of travelling abroad (Thailand and Sri Lanka) without permission. He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."
Article Summary: The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma. The non-commissioned IAF officer had served about 10 and a half years. He had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.

Article Title: Safai Karmachari Andolan counters govt reply in Parliament, claims manual scavenging still exists in atleast 46 districts
Article Text:
Muzaffar Ahmed Sheikh (35) from Ganderbal district in Jammu & Kashmir.

Mussi Devi (71) from Sitapur district in Uttar Pradesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Challenging the Centre’s claim made in Parliament in the monsoon session that a survey conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 found no person engaged as a manual scavenger, Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) on Tuesday brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and youth from Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines to highlight that the illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.National Convenor and co-founder of SKA, Bezwada Wilson said that they have evidence by way of photographs showing women lifting waste from dry latrines in these districts. “We will be writing to the ministry of social justice and empowerment to seek a fresh survey citing this evidence and demand action to stop the illegal practice in these districts within 60 days,” Wilson said.He, however, made it clear that if the ministry fails to act over the next two months, SKA teams will carry out a survey and put together a report by early next year. “We will highlight the findings across states and share them with Parliamentarians and the Judiciary to seek enforcement,” Wilson said.Former Supreme Court Judges Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Sudhandhu Dhulia and former Patna High Court Judge Justice Anjana Prakash expressed solidarity with the women and men who came forward to share heartwrenching experiences of a life marked by exploitation and untouchability despite the law in place wherein manual scavenging is illegal and dry latrines are banned.At the meeting held at Press Club of India as SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging, the former judges announced full support. Elaborating on the struggle by those involved in manual scavenging to break free, Justice Lokur expressed concern over the practice persisting despite the protection guaranteed by the Constitution of India against untouchability which is abolished and forbidden.He also dwelled on the long and continuing struggle for justice by those affected and how they have repeatedly ended up approaching the judiciary that has resulted in various directions from the Supreme Court from time to time. Justice Lokur highlighted that what is most worrying is the denial by authorities that the problem exists and the approach towards addressing the issue shows that ending the problem of manual scavenging is not a priority of the govt.He asserted that the govt must give priority to remove dry latrines wherever they remain. This he said should be a key focus area under the Swachh Bharat Mission.Justice Dhulia expressed shock that manual scavenging and dry latrines still exist in more than 40 districts and said that everyone must feel shame that such a practice continues to exist in our society.Justice Anjana Prakash too expressed concern over the lack of required efforts to end manual scavenging.As the workers shared their lived experiences as manual scavengers, one heard 71 - year - old Mussi Devi from Sitapur district in UP tell how her entire life has passed cleaning dry latrines and even now she is called by families in her area to manually clean-up and dispose of the waste. “When are we going to get freedom from this untouchability?,” asked Mussi Devi and others in her position. Ageing and frail, Devi is also the caregiver for her husband who is paralysed.35 - year - old Muzzafar Ahmed Sheikh from Jammu and Kashmir shared that he is the third generation in his family engaged in manual scavenging in dry latrines. He shared that his community is subjected to untouchability and even their houses are located in a separate cluster. He hails from Wussan village of Ganderbal. A father of a six - year - old, he says, “I want to break free from this identity of being a manual scavenger and I don’t want my son to grow up to do this ever. ”Bezwada Wilson summed up the sentiment of all those seeking justice. “I started the fight when I was 16 and now I am 60. Many things have changed but manual scavenging in dry latrines still remains. We have to end this menace without fail,” he asserted.It is pertinent to point that in the monsoon session of Parliament that concluded in August, in response to a written question in Lok Sabha by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale said that as per the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)", a fresh survey has been conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 in which no manual scavenger has been found. “All the districts of the country have completed the survey and declared themselves as manual scavengers' free,” he said.However, he also added that 58,098 Manual Scavengers (MS) have been identified during two earlier surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018.Clearly differentiating "manual scavenging" and "hazardous cleaning", the minister shared while the later pertains to manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank, without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices and safety precautions, a manual scavenger is defined as someone employed for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of human excreta in an insanitary latrine.
Article Summary: Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines. The illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states. SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging.

Article Title: BJP vs SP ahead of 2027 UP polls: Akhilesh shares AI video of CM Yogi; BJP hits back
Article Text:
CM Yogi, Akhilesh Yadav

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, the political battle between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Samajwadi Party (SP) has intensified with AI-generated songs and videos.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav shared an AI-generated video targeting Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath , drawing a sharp response from the BJP.The latest exchange began after BJP-backed social media handles circulated an AI-generated song targeting Akhilesh Yadav, calling him "Teepu" and accusing his government of presiding over lawlessness.The song featured the lyrics: “UP badnaam hua, Teepu tere maare… (UP has become infamous because of Teepu).” The accompanying video used an AI-generated depiction of the SP chief.In response to this, the Samjawadi Party media cell on Monday shared an AI-generated video targeting CM Yogi Adityanath, referring to him as "Baba". The video featured AI-generated visuals of the Uttar Pradesh CM and took aim at the state government over issues including unemployment and alleged paper leaks.The song used the line, “UP badnaam hua, Baba tere maare… (UP has become infamous because of Baba)”.Akhilesh has frequently referred to Adityanath as "Baba" while attacking the chief minister politically.“If the BJP uses AI to make songs targeting me, we will also respond to those songs with songs,” Akhilesh said.The SP chief also alleged that AI-generated videos were being created and circulated to defame opposition leaders. He cautioned the government against using artificial intelligence for such purposes and claimed that the SP would outpace the BJP in the use of the technology if such a battle continued.The Samajwadi Party media cell also warned the BJP against using AI to target the party."Listen, BJP folks Stop playing this childish, deceptive game with AI; the socialists haven't even started playing the real game yet, Look here, brother, this is social media—if you start it, we've got a full accounting of your 10 years, you'll make one, and our creative workers and socialist supporters will pour cold water on everything you've done For now, take this first response; you won't even be able to handle the next one"Reacting to the AI-generated video targeting Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh minister Dayashankar Singh accused the SP of trying to create an atmosphere of tension ahead of the 2027 elections."The Samajwadi Party feels its defeat in 2027 is certain, so by doing things like this, they want to spoil the atmosphere, in view of the development that has taken place in Uttar Pradesh and the pace of development in the country under PM Modi's leadership. The BJP won with a thumping majority in Haryana, Maharashtra, Delhi, Bihar, Bengal... Now elections are happening in Uttar Pradesh, PM Modi and Yogi ji are here; a tsunami is going to sweep here. In frustration, the Samajwadi Party is doing such things."
Article Summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav shared an AI-generated video targeting Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath. The video took aim at the state government over issues including unemployment and alleged paper leaks. Uttar Pradesh minister Dayashankar Singh accused the SP of trying to create an atmosphere of tension ahead of 2027 elections.

Article Title: Kanye West questions what Lewis Hamilton sees in Kim Kardashian as their romance draws scrutiny
Article Text:
Lewis Hamilton faces warning.(Image via Getty Images)

Kanye West shares blunt view on Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian

Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton’s reported romance draws attention

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kanye West has sparked fresh attention around Kim Kardashian’s reported romance with Lewis Hamilton after sharing his blunt opinion about the Formula 1 champion’s relationship with his former wife. West questioned Hamilton’s decision to date Kardashian, pointing to her four children and his own experience of their marriage. His remarks have added another layer of intrigue to a relationship that has attracted intense public interest throughout 2026.West did not hold back when asked about Hamilton and Kardashian. His comments focused less on the Formula 1 star’s fame and more on the realities of entering a relationship with someone who already has a family.“Honestly, I don’t understand how some guys think. I wish Lewis had someone who could give him some good advice, but apparently, he doesn’t. I just can’t understand how, at his age and with everything he’s accomplished, he’d choose to date a woman who already has four children with another man and be completely comfortable with that.“I’ve already experienced that relationship and everything that came with it, and to be honest, it’s nothing special, which makes me wonder what he sees in it.But he seems completely comfortable with the situation, and I guess that’s what matters to him. Personally, though, it’s not something I would ever choose for myself again.”The comments carry added weight because West and Kardashian were married for almost seven years. Kardashian filed for divorce in February 2021, and their divorce was finalised in November 2022. They share four children, with their settlement including joint custody and arrangements for shared expenses.West’s perspective also comes from having lived through the pressures that come with being part of the Kardashian family. His comments therefore offer a deeply personal view, although Hamilton’s reported relationship with Kardashian remains his own.Hamilton and Kardashian have known each other for years. Their paths first crossed around 2014, when they attended the GQ Men of the Year Awards in London with their respective partners at the time.Their friendship continued as they moved through overlapping worlds of sport, fashion and entertainment. However, speculation about a possible romance intensified in 2026 after they were reportedly seen together during the New Year period in Aspen.Further appearances fueled the conversation. The pair were linked to trips and public outings, including time in Paris and at major entertainment and sporting events. Hamilton also appeared in content connected to Kardashian, while Kardashian was later seen supporting him at the Monaco Grand Prix.Their connection became even more closely watched after Hamilton reportedly spent part of the Fourth of July holiday with Kardashian and her family in Idaho. Reports also suggested that he had developed a comfortable relationship with her children.For now, the reported romance continues to command attention because of the people involved. Hamilton is one of Formula 1’s most accomplished stars, while Kardashian remains a major figure in entertainment and business. West’s latest comments have simply pushed their already high-profile relationship back into the spotlight.
Article Summary: Kanye West questions Lewis Hamilton's decision to date Kim Kardashian. West and Kardashian were married for almost seven years. The pair share four children, with their settlement including joint custody and arrangements for shared expenses. Hamilton and Kardashian have known each other for years.

Article Title: Tom Brady's wealth skyrockets as his $500 million Las Vegas Raiders investment grows ahead of new season
Article Text:
Tom Brady's wealth.(Image via Getty Images)

Tom Brady’s wealth grows as his investment in the Las Vegas Raiders continues to increase its value ahead of the new season

Tom Brady makes it clear what he is focusing on ahead of the new season

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was one of the greatest athletes in the world whose personal life has dominated headlines throughout his career. While Tom Brady is already a multi millionaire, it seems his wealth has increased more in the last few weeks.As per reports, Tom Brady’s investment in the Las Vegas Raiders has grown significantly in the last few weeks.As per Celebrity Net Worth, Tom Brady’s 5% share in the team is roughly worth a whopping $500 million since the Las Vegas Raiders is now valued at a whopping $10 billion.Back in October 2024, Tom Brady and Knighthead Capital Management co-founder Tom Wagner purchased a combined 10% stake in the Las Vegas Raiders for a whopping $220 million. Out of this, the NFL legend owns a 5% stake in the team.A few months ago, in an interview with CNBC, Tom Brady opened up about his stake in the Las Vegas Raiders as he said, “I’m a minority owner. So, when you’re that, there’s really no job description. I don’t really have a daily role…”The seven time Super Bowl champion added, “You know, my phone call is always available to everybody who needs it. I want to see everyone succeed, be their best, bring a winning kind of a culture to Las Vegas — to bring the Raiders back to glory.I’d love to be a part of it.”Back in August 2025, the Las Vegas Raiders' estimated value had already climbed to about $7.7 billion which again increased by May 2026.While Tom Brady has only gotten more and more wealthier in the last few years, his only focus has been his children.A few years ago, in an interview, Tom Brady opened up about fatherhood as he said, "I'm 44. I've got a family that I'm a dad to some amazing children…When I think about being a dad, I think about him because of what my dad meant to me, and I know I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad's been to me.”The star player added, “And I use them as my example as to how to keep a family together and to care and to support and to love."The seven time Super Bowl champion added, "We want our kids to be happy. I want them to be respectful of people. I want them to be kind. I wanna make the world a better place." However, he also expressed his hope that his children learn from his experience.
Article Summary: Tom Brady’s investment in the Las Vegas Raiders has grown significantly in the last few weeks. The NFL legend owns a 5% stake in the team which is now valued at a whopping $10 billion. The seven time Super Bowl champion opened up about fatherhood as he said, "We want our kids to be happy"

Ahead of the new season, the LeBron James Family Foundation has also marked another milestone for children in Ohio.A few weeks ago, the LeBron James Family Foundation’s education wing, the I PROMISE School collaborated with Nike for their fourth year in helping children to learn how to swim.In a heartfelt post, the I PROMISE School posted, “Watching our @ipromiseschool students grow in confidence never gets old. 💙 For the fourth straight summer, @nikeswim camp is helping our students learn a skill that can change lives. 🏊Throughout the week we saw first-time swimmers overcome their fears, returning swimmers step into leadership roles to help their peers, and our students discovered confidence they didn’t know they had. 🙌”The post added, “A special thank you to Nike, Firestone High School swim team, and @ussportscamps for opening their doors and creating new opportunities for our kids. Article Title: 140 kmph, Rs 21.5 lakh and a dream: Shubham Gautam's rise from Narora
Article Text:
Shubham Gautam

Shubham Gautam with his coach Ankit Kumar Rajput at their academy in Narora, in the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh.

He has always had this good athletic body. He came to our academy when he was 14, and from that age, you could sense that the boy was different from the others. Ankit Kumar Rajput

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shubham Gautam hails from Narora, a town located on the banks of the Ganga River in the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh. Narora is famous for its nuclear power plant, operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).In the NPCIL campus, Ankit Kumar Rajput runs a cricket academy, where he first spotted Shubham Gautam, a fast bowler who earlier this year won the speed hunt organised by the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) and went on to become one of the most expensive players in the UPT20 League when Noida Kings roped him in for Rs 21.50 lakh."He has always had this good athletic body. He came to our academy when he was 14, and from that age, you could sense that the boy was different from the others," Rajput, Gautam's coach, tells TimesofIndia.com.Rajput says it is not easy for cricketers to break out from Narora, and Shubham has been an anomaly."It is one of the most backward areas of Uttar Pradesh. Cricket-wise also, you don't see anyone pursuing the sport once they pass their Class XII boards. Shubham has been different. He has been picked for the UP U-19 camps a couple of times. It was just that he never made the cut, but he was very serious about his cricket. He kept chasing his dream, and now he is living it.For someone from our area to be able to play cricket at the professional level, one needs to be special, and he is," says a proud coach.Gautam, 21, has not yet set the Uttar Pradesh T20 League on fire. The playing XI combination hasn't helped, as he has featured in only four games so far, but he has consistently hit the 140 kmph mark in the 12 overs he has bowled in the tournament.But for Gautam, it is not a big deal because he has always had to wait for his chances."I played district cricket but never played for Uttar Pradesh at the age-group level. I used to play tennis-ball cricket, and I started playing with a leather ball in 2017. Every year, I used to reach the final round in the trials, but this time I put in more effort. That helped me get this opportunity," he narrates his journey to this website."My father is a farmer, and farming these days is not easy. But he always supported my dream, and I guess being the youngest among the four siblings also helped me," he says.The windfall at the UPT20 auction has changed the fortunes of Gautam."I never imagined that I would go for such a big amount at the auction. I was tired and sleeping when the auction was happening, and then I found out about it. To be honest, I was a bit emotional," says Gautam, who idolises Jofra Archer For Gautam, bowling quick and making batters dance to his tunes with his length is something that he cherishes the most."Jofra Archer is the fast bowler who inspires me the most," he says."My strength is my pace, but I have also learnt to hit the right lengths. In UPT20, I have seen that if you miss your length, batters can hit the ball from one place and send it out of the ground from another," he adds.Recently, it has been a lot of firsts for Gautam."Before this, I had only played day-night matches in private tournaments. I had never played in a league like this. My focus is on doing well in these matches. If I perform well here, it will help me in the future. My next aim is to play for Uttar Pradesh," he says.Back in Narora, Ankit Kumar Rajput, who has seen Gautam's rise from close quarters, says his ward playing in the UP League has increased the number of players at his academy."Narora has a cricketing hero now," laughs Rajput.Ankit shares an interesting story about Gautam, which tells a lot about the individual the youngster is."He never had a phone. The first one he got was two years ago, and that too in a tournament held in Aligarh, where he was the best bowler. He has always been a hustler, and in the future, you will hear a lot about him," he says.
Article Summary: Fast bowler Shubham Gautam hails from Narora, in Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh. He won the speed hunt organised by the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) and went on to become one of the most expensive players in the UPT20 League when Noida Kings roped him in for Rs 21.50 lakh.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My mom has been my rock through everything” - How Coco Gauff turned family sacrifices, a leap of faith, and unshakeable belief into Grand Slam glory
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My mom has been my rock through everything” - How Coco Gauff turned family sacrifices, a leap of faith, and unshakeable belief into Grand Slam glory

How did Corey and Candi Gauff change their lives for Coco Gauff’s tennis dream

How did Coco Gauff’s family help her handle fame after beating Venus Williams

How did Coco Gauff’s parents react when she won the 2023 US Open

Why does Coco Gauff’s family story still matter beyond her tennis career

Coco Gauff’s rise to Grand Slam glory was built long before she lifted the US Open trophy. Her parents, Corey and Candi Gauff, changed their lives to give their daughter a better chance in tennis, moving the family from Atlanta to Delray Beach, Florida, when Coco was still a child. Corey stepped away from his career to coach her, while Candi took charge of her homeschooling. Years later, after Coco became a major tennis star, she continued to point back to the same people who believed in her before the world did. For her, family was never separate from the journey.Coco Gauff’s tennis journey took a serious turn when she was still very young. Her parents had both been college athletes - Corey played basketball at Georgia State University, while Candi competed in track and field at Florida State University. They understood what training and competition demanded, but they also knew that their daughter needed the right environment if she wanted to see how far tennis could take her.The family eventually moved from Atlanta back to Delray Beach, where Corey and Candi had grown up. Better tennis opportunities were a major reason for the decision. The move also meant giving up the stability they had built in Atlanta. The family initially stayed with Coco’s maternal grandparents before getting their own home.ESPN reported that Corey left his healthcare career and became Coco’s coach, while Candi left education to homeschool her daughter.That was not a small change for a family with three children. Coco had to train seriously while continuing her education at home, and her parents had to organize their lives around her development. Corey handled much of the tennis work, while Candi made sure school did not disappear from the picture.Coco has spoken about how much that early belief meant to her. She recalled:“We realized Florida was the place to be for tennis, so we moved from Atlanta. My parents gave up their dream house. We stayed with my grandmother for six, seven months before we could get our own place… My dad told me I could do it when I was eight years old. Obviously, you’re never 100% sure, but my parents believed in me from the start. That belief meant everything when I was growing up.”The next major change came in 2019, when Coco Gauff became a global name at just 15. She entered Wimbledon as a qualifier and then defeated five-time champion Venus Williams in the first round. The win changed the scale of attention around her almost overnight.There were suddenly questions about how far she could go, whether she could become the next big American tennis star and how quickly she could win major titles. For a teenager, that attention could easily become overwhelming.Her family tried to keep tennis in its proper place. Candi, in particular, reminded Coco that being a tennis player was only one part of who she was. That message mattered because Coco was learning to deal with victories, losses, interviews and expectations while still growing up.Speaking about her mother’s influence, Gauff said:“My mom always tells me to just be Coco. She reminds me that tennis is just a game, and it doesn’t define who I am as a person. Having that perspective from my family keeps me sane. Win or lose, they love me the exact same way.”That approach gave Coco something outside the results. A bad match could hurt, but it did not change how her family saw her. That distinction became especially important as the attention around her grew.The biggest reward for years of work arrived at the 2023 US Open. Gauff, then 19, defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the final to win her first Grand Slam singles title. She lost the opening set but fought back to win the match in three sets, completing one of the biggest victories of her young career.For Coco, the win was also a personal answer to the disappointment she had carried from her first Grand Slam final at the French Open in 2022. She had lost that match to Iga Swiatek, but the defeat became part of the road that led her to New York.After beating Sabalenka, Gauff spoke about the people who had stayed with her through every stage of that journey. Her parents were at the centre of that message.“Thank you to my parents. Today was the first time I ever saw my dad cry. He doesn’t want me to tell you that, but he did! He supported me from day one. My mom, she’s been my rock through everything. I’m just so grateful for them.”She also had a message for the people who had doubted her:“To those who thought they were putting water on my fire, you were really adding gas to it. Now I’m burning so bright.”The words were personal because the road to that trophy had not been smooth. Her family had made difficult choices when she was a child, and Coco had spent years trying to turn their faith into results.Coco Gauff’s success is easy to explain through her talent, speed and fighting spirit. But her story also shows what happened away from the centre court. Her parents made major changes before there was any guarantee that their daughter would become a professional player.They did not simply put Coco into a tennis programme and wait for results. Corey coached her, Candi handled her education, and the family adjusted its daily life around her training. Coco also grew up with her younger brothers, Cody and Cameron, keeping family life separate from the pressure of competition.That balance became especially valuable after her breakthrough at Wimbledon. TIME reported that Gauff’s move to Delray Beach gave her access to better tennis training while homeschooling allowed greater flexibility around practice.Her first Grand Slam title therefore meant more than a trophy. It was the result of years of decisions made when there was no certainty about the outcome.Coco Gauff is now an established name in American tennis, but the foundation of her career was built when she was still a child. Her parents believed in the possibility before the titles arrived. Coco’s own words about them show why their role continues to be such an important part of her story.
Article Summary: Coco Gauff won her first Grand Slam singles title at the 2023 US Open. Her parents, Corey and Candi, changed their lives to give their daughter a better chance. Corey left his healthcare career and became Coco’s coach, while Candi left education to homeschool her daughter.

Despite emergency treatment and intensive efforts to save him, Sorrell’s condition became too severe. His loved ones are now dealing with grief while also trying to understand how a young athlete could be lost so suddenly.His family said doctors believe an underlying genetic condition may have contributed to his death. No specific condition has been identified publicly, and his cause of death has not been officially disclosed. His four siblings are expected to undergo testing as the family seeks more information.The school community learned of Sorrell’s death on Sunday. Principal CeCe Matson shared a message of grief with families and students.“Today, our Northwest Middle School family is grieving the loss of one of our students. Article Title: Fastest century in cricket: Why Percy Fender’s 35-minute first-class hundred from 1920 remains unbeaten after 106 years
Article Text:
Percy Fender (Pic credit: PA Images/Alamy)

Fender turns Northamptonshire attack into record

Fender went on to score 113 in 42 minutes

The 1983 century that matched Fender — but did not count

Why faster centuries are not recognised

Fastest centuries depend on how ‘fastest’ is measured

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The fastest century in first-class cricket by time spent at the crease was scored more than a century ago, yet the record remains intact. Percy Fender smashed his hundred in just 35 minutes for Surrey against Northamptonshire at Northampton on August 26, 1920 — and despite several later centuries being completed in less time, none have been accepted as a genuine challenge to his mark.Fender’s record has survived because cricket’s record books make an important distinction between a breathtaking batting assault and a century produced in deliberately staged circumstances.Steve O’Shaughnessy equalled Fender’s 35-minute mark for Lancashire against Leicestershire in 1983, while centuries have since been timed at even quicker rates. But those performances came in matches where the bowling and circumstances were manipulated to force a result or achieve specific objectives.As a result, Fender’s 35-minute hundred remains widely regarded as the fastest authentic first-class century in terms of time taken.Four days after his 28th birthday, Fender walked out for Surrey in a County Championship match that would become one of the most remarkable batting spectacles of his career.Northamptonshire made 306 in their first innings, with Fanny Walden scoring 128. Fender contributed with the ball, taking three wickets.Surrey initially found themselves in trouble at 160 for four after Andy Sandham fell for 92. But Andy Ducat and Alan Peach transformed the innings, adding 288 in just 135 minutes. Ducat eventually fell for 149, leaving Fender to take centre stage.What followed was extraordinary.Fender attacked almost from the moment he arrived, unleashing booming drives, fierce cuts, pulls and trademark slashes. He raced to his fifty in just 19 minutes, with Northamptonshire struggling to find a way of slowing him down.Gilbert Jessop had previously held the record for the fastest first-class century, reaching three figures in 40 minutes against Yorkshire at Harrogate in 1897.Fender went five minutes faster. He eventually reached his century in 35 minutes.Fender did not slow down after reaching the landmark.He finished unbeaten on 113 from 42 minutes, hitting 16 fours and five sixes. Remarkably, 94 of his 113 runs came in boundaries, meaning more than 83 per cent of his score came from fours and sixes.Surrey declared once Peach reached his double-century. Peach finished unbeaten on 203, while the sixth-wicket pair had added 171 runs in only 42 minutes.The speed of Fender’s innings was extraordinary even by modern T20 standards.Yet the record is not simply about how many balls Fender faced. It is specifically a record for the time elapsed while the batter was at the crease, an older method of measuring batting speed that differs from modern balls-faced records.That distinction is crucial when discussing the “fastest century” in cricket.For 63 years, Fender stood alone. Then came Steve O’Shaughnessy.The Lancashire all-rounder scored a century in 35 minutes against Leicestershire in 1983, apparently matching Fender’s record. But the circumstances surrounding the innings made it impossible to treat it as an equivalent achievement.The match had been disrupted by bad weather, with play beginning late. By the final day, both teams had specific incentives to accelerate proceedings.After Leicestershire declared, O’Shaughnessy and Graeme Fowler walked out for Lancashire against an attack that included David Gower and James Whitaker.What followed was described as farcical.Gower and Whitaker bowled a succession of full tosses and long hops, while the short boundary made attacking cricket even easier. Fowler smashed 100, including 10 sixes, while O’Shaughnessy also raced to three figures.He reached his century in 35 minutes — but the innings was effectively produced under manufactured conditions designed to accelerate scoring.O’Shaughnessy was not the only batter to score faster than Fender.Glen Chapple hit a century in 21 minutes for Lancashire against Glamorgan in 1993. Mark Pettini scored one in 24 minutes for Essex against Leicestershire in 2006, while Michael Goodwin and Tom Moody also produced centuries in 25 and 26 minutes respectively.But these innings belong to the category of centuries that do not count for the genuine time-based record.Manufactured declarations and deliberately friendly bowling were once a feature of County Championship cricket, particularly when matches were played over three days. Captains sometimes had to find extraordinary ways of creating enough time for a result after weather interruptions or slow play.Part-time bowlers delivering full tosses and long hops could turn an innings into a boundary-hitting exercise. Although the runs officially counted in the match scorecard, records created under such conditions have generally been regarded as staged and unsuitable for comparison.That leaves Fender’s 1920 performance as the benchmark.There is another important distinction.If “fastest century” is measured by balls faced, rather than time spent at the crease, the first-class record belongs to David Hookes, who scored 102 from just 34 balls for South Australia against Victoria in 1982.In Test cricket, Brendon McCullum holds the record, scoring his century from 54 balls against Australia in Christchurch in 2016.But by elapsed time in genuine first-class conditions, Fender remains the man to beat.More than 100 years after he unleashed his extraordinary attack on Northamptonshire, no legitimate first-class innings has bettered his 35-minute mark.And that is why, despite several faster-looking centuries appearing in the record books, Percy Fender’s 35-minute hundred from 1920 remains the gold standard for the fastest authentic first-class century by time.
Article Summary: Percy Fender scored 113 in just 35 minutes for Surrey against Northamptonshire in August 1920. Steve O’Shaughnessy equalled Fender’s 35-minute mark for Lancashire against Leicestershire in 1983. But those performances came in matches where bowling and circumstances were manipulated to force a result or achieve specific objectives.

Article Title: What’s going on with Tony Romo? Ex-Dallas Cowboys quarterback makes candid confession about “over-reliance on alcohol”
Article Text:
Tony Romo. Image via: Getty Images

Tony Romo makes confession about “over-reliance on alcohol”

Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI charge, issues apology

Romo looks ahead to health, family and CBS return

Tony Romo has opened up about his personal struggle after pleading no contest to a civil OWI offense in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback admitted he has been dealing with an alcohol problem, linking it to years of pain following multiple back surgeries. Romo addressed the situation publicly on Instagram, accepting responsibility for his actions and explaining how his dependence on pain medication eventually shifted toward alcohol. His statement was unusually candid for a former NFL star who has spent years in the public eye as one of football’s most recognizable broadcasters.Romo’s comments came after his July 23 arrest in Milwaukee County. The 46-year-old was facing multiple citations following a traffic stop, including operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing and possessing an open intoxicant. He has now accepted the consequences of the OWI offense while also outlining the steps he is taking to address his health. His driving privileges have been revoked for six months, and he must complete an alcohol assessment program.Tony Romo’s statement focused less on the legal case and more on the personal road that led him there.The former Cowboys quarterback said multiple back surgeries ended his playing career earlier than expected and left him dealing with “constant, debilitating pain.”He explained that the pain first led to dependence on medication. His efforts to stop taking those medications eventually resulted in what he described as an “over-reliance on alcohol.”Romo did not present his history as an excuse. Instead, he accepted responsibility while explaining the circumstances behind his struggles.“As I have told my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward.”He also said he is working closely with a team of doctors to address his health. Romo thanked his family, friends and members of the NFL community for supporting him during a difficult period.Among those offering support was Tom Brady, who joined others in responding to Romo’s Instagram post.Romo pleaded no contest to the OWI offense on Sept. 1, bringing a significant development in the legal matter that began with his July arrest.Court records show his driving privileges were revoked for six months. He was also ordered to complete an alcohol assessment program and pay $834 in fines. An ignition interlock device must be installed on vehicles owned, operated or registered in his name, with the requirement lasting for at least one year after his license is reissued.The other citations connected to the arrest were dismissed.Romo was stopped while driving southbound on Interstate 43 after reportedly being observed making an unsafe pass. According to the supplied records, he performed poorly on standard field sobriety tests. Body camera footage later showed Romo telling deputies he had been coming from a golf tournament and was heading to visit his grandparents.The arrest came after Romo had competed in the Wisconsin Amateur Championship earlier that day. He finished tied for 73rd.The legal consequences are only one part of the situation for Romo. His immediate focus is now on his health and family.“The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant,” Romo said. “It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public.”He also made clear he wants privacy while working through the situation.“As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.”Romo has been on leave from CBS since July 31. J.J. Watt is set to join Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on the network’s lead NFL broadcast team during his absence.For Romo, the next chapter is less about football than it is about addressing a problem he has now acknowledged publicly and taking the steps he believes are necessary to move forward.
Article Summary: Tony Romo has opened up about his personal struggle after pleading no contest to a civil OWI offense in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback admitted he has been dealing with an alcohol problem. Romo addressed the situation publicly on Instagram, accepting responsibility for his actions and explaining how his dependence on pain medication eventually shifted toward alcohol.

Article Title: NBA roster update: Philadelphia 76ers bring in 7-foot-6 star to support LeBron James’ championship dream
Article Text:
Tacko Fall. Image via: Adam Pantozzi/National Basketball Association via Getty Images

Philadelphia 76ers sign Tacko Fall and two other stars

Why Philadelphia made the move

LeBron James is serious about a Philadelphia 76ers championship

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tacko Fall is heading back to the NBA. The 7-foot-6 center has signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, giving him a shot to earn a roster spot when training camp opens in New Jersey later this month.It's a modest move on paper, but it lands during arguably the busiest offseason in franchise history, one that already brought in LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. And if Fall sticks around past camp, sharing a locker room with James would be one of the more unexpected subplots of his NBA return.Tacko Fall, 30, hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season with Cleveland. Across parts of three seasons with the Celtics and Cavaliers, he appeared in 37 games and averaged 2.2 points, 2.4 rebounds and 6.2 minutes. Since then, he's played overseas, most recently with the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association, and he spent last season with the New Zealand Breakers, averaging 11.4 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.6 blocks over 18 games.He isn't arriving alone. Guard Jameer Nelson Jr. and forward Saint Thomas also signed Exhibit 10 contracts, with terms undisclosed. The team confirmed the moves directly: "We have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr.,and Saint Thomas," the Sixers posted on X.Nelson, 25, averaged 18.9 points and 3.4 assists last season with the G League's Stockton Kings. He's the son of longtime NBA guard Jameer Nelson, who now serves as the Sixers' executive vice president of basketball operations. Thomas, 23, spent last season with Philadelphia's G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats, putting up 12.5 points and 5.0 rebounds a game before appearing in four Summer League contests for the Sixers this year.None of the three is likely to make a real dent in the rotation, and making the roster at all is far from guaranteed. Philadelphia enters camp with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Brown and James all on the roster, and questions about outside shooting, defensive versatility and health, particularly around Embiid and a 41-year-old James, haven't gone away. Head coach Nick Nurse will be the one tasked with making the fit work. The Sixers open their regular season on October 20 against the Knicks.James is entering his 24th NBA season, his first with the Sixers after eight years with the Lakers that included a championship in 2020. He's said the chance to compete for another title, not money, is what pulled him to Philadelphia.On August 31, he posted an Instagram story of himself shirtless and sweating through a workout, writing "It's just WORK!!" before flashing a goofy grin at the camera. It's a familiar move for James, who's built a career partly on showing his offseason grind, and the clip spread quickly online.He's already logging time with new teammates. Brown described a recent session in Los Angeles with James and Maxey under trainer Chris Johnson during a Twitch stream: "I've been working, building chemistry with the guys." He added that the energy and talent in the room were obvious, though he was careful not to get ahead of himself about what it all means once the season starts.
Article Summary: Tacko Fall has signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 30-year-old center hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season with Cleveland. Guard Jameer Nelson Jr. and forward Saint Thomas also signed Exhibit 10 contracts, with terms undisclosed.

Article Title: “I was ultimately trying to see both”: How Donna Kelce’s 1,300-mile journey to Jason and Travis Kelce’s games became an unforgettable mother-son moment
Article Text:
How Donna Kelce’s 1,300-mile journey to Jason and Travis Kelce’s games became an unforgettable mother-son moment(Getty)

How did Donna Kelce make it from Jason Kelce’s Eagles game to Travis Kelce’s Chiefs game?

Why did Travis Kelce’s postgame exchange with Donna make the journey unforgettable?

Donna Kelce had two sons playing playoff football on January 16, 2022, and their games were nearly 1,300 miles apart. Jason Kelce’s Philadelphia Eagles faced the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Florida, while Travis Kelce ’s Kansas City Chiefs hosted the Pittsburgh Steelers that night. Donna did not pick one son. She watched Jason first, then raced across the country to reach Travis.It was a hectic trip from start to finish. Donna dealt with a rickshaw, an Uber, a delayed flight and rain before reaching Kansas City. She arrived during the Chiefs game, but the long day gave her something far more memorable than a simple trip between stadiums. It gave her a chance to be there for both sons.Donna Kelce began January 16 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, where Jason Kelce and the Eagles faced Tom Brady and the Buccaneers in the NFC Wild Card round. Philadelphia struggled from the start and eventually fell 31-15, ending Jason's season. Donna, however, could not stay in Tampa for long.Travis Kelce and the Chiefs were scheduled to play the Pittsburgh Steelers at Arrowhead Stadium that evening. The Eagles kicked off at 1 p.m. ET, while Kansas City's game started at 8:15 p.m. ET, leaving Donna only a few hours to get from Florida to Missouri.After Jason Kelce's game, Donna began the second leg of her journey. She told the NFL that she had to use a rickshaw to reach her Uber pickup area at the stadium.Her flight then faced a 30-minute delay, and rain made the trip even more difficult. Still, Donna kept moving and eventually reached Kansas City.The NFL followed her journey throughout the day. At one point, Donna wrote, “One game down, one to go! Headed to the airport!” She later updated fans from the car on the way to Arrowhead.Donna finally made it into the stadium during the Chiefs game. She missed Travis' 48-yard touchdown catch just before halftime because she was still traveling, but she arrived in time to watch the rest of his impressive night. Travis finished with five catches for 108 yards and a touchdown as Kansas City beat Pittsburgh 42-21. He also threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Byron Pringle in the fourth quarter.After the Chiefs' win on January 16, Donna still had one more moment with Travis. She appeared during his postgame news conference and was introduced as the next person to ask a question. Travis initially sounded confused before realizing his mother was on the call.Donna asked how it felt to throw his first NFL touchdown. The question took Travis back to something he had told her as a child.“Man, to finally throw a touchdown like I used to tell my mom when I was like five years old, that I was going to eventually throw a touchdown in the National Football League,” Travis said during the Chiefs' postgame news conference. “I finally got it done, it only took me nine years.”Donna then put the entire day into perspective with her own response. “That's what makes sports so great, because you can be depressed in the morning and elated in the evening,” she told Travis during the postgame exchange.Donna spoke with WKYC's Jay Crawford about the journey. She explained that the goal had always been simple.“I was ultimately trying to see both of the games and it worked out,” Donna said during the WKYC interview.It did. She watched Jason Kelce's Eagles in Tampa, then crossed the country to see Travis Kelce's Chiefs in Kansas City. Jason's team lost, Travis' team won, but Donna never treated the two games differently. For her, the victory was simply making sure both sons saw their mother in the stands that day.
