Article Title: How ABVP retained Panjab University presidency with just one more vote than last year
Article Text:
Jubilant ABVP candidates and their supporters celebrate their win





CHANDIGARH: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad’s ( ABVP ) second successive presidential victory at Panjab University was shaped by a combination of organisational unity, the return of last year’s breakaway faction to the campaign fold, influence of large voting departments and a divided field of rivals.ABVP’s Ankit secured 3,149 votes, defeating ASAP’s (Association of Students for Alternative Politics) Aadil Brar, who polled 2,637. NSUI ’s (National Students’ Union of India) Gurman Singh Sidhu secured 2,263 votes, while SATH’s Darshpreet Singh got 1,387.ASAP entered the contest with considerable political firepower, with AAP MP Meet Hayer and MLA Amritpal Singh Sukhanand handling its campaign. NSUI, meanwhile, received public backing from senior Congress leaders, including Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.ABVP’s advantage was continuity. It had an organisation that had already won the presidency, a campaign team with experience and a candidate who was not new to campus politics.Among the four presidential candidates, Ankit was the only contender apart from Darshpreet to have been visible in PU politics for several years. Aadil Brar, though a relatively fresh presidential face, had served as UILS department representative and had an established campus network.Gurman was the freshest of the principal contenders — a disadvantage in an election where name recognition, personal networks and mobilisation can matter as much as party labels.The biggest change, however, came within ABVP itself. Last year, the breakaway ABVP Front had contested separately, with its candidate Naveen Kumar finishing second in the vice-president race with 2,828 votes. This time, several of those who had emerged as potential kingmakers were back in the ABVP campaign.Former PU ABVP campus president Rajat Puri, Political Science research scholar Vishal Malik, former UILS student Saksham Sharma and outgoing PUCSC president Gaurav Veer Sohal were actively involved. North Zone organising secretary Gaurav Attri, under whose organisational charge ABVP won its first PU presidency last year, was again involved.Significantly, ABVP did not need to increase its presidential vote. Ankit’s 3,149 votes were just one more than Sohal’s 3,148 last year. The total presidential votes, including NOTA, were also almost unchanged — 9,610 this year against 9,613 last year.What changed was the configuration around that vote. Last year’s eight-cornered contest allowed multiple candidates to occupy different pockets of the anti-ABVP vote. This year, the field was reduced to four, concentrating the contest but leaving the opposition split among ASAP, NSUI and SATH. ABVP was therefore able to retain roughly one-third of the presidential vote.
Article Summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad’s ( ABVP ) second successive presidential victory at Panjab University was shaped by a combination of organisational unity, the return of last year's breakaway faction to the campaign fold, influence of large voting departments and a divided field of rivals. The biggest change, however, came within ABVP itself.

Article Title: Amid row, Chhattisgarh judge named as Rajasthan HC Chief Justice
Article Text:
The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal as Chief Justice for Rajasthan High Court.





JAIPUR: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal of Chhattisgarh HC as Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC late Monday, ending a nearly yearlong stint under acting CJ Sanjeev Prakash Sharma as protests by lawyers over his functioning intensified. The Collegium also recommended Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as CJ of J&K HC.Hours before the recommendation, Sharma decided to abstain from judicial work from Sept 1 to 5. Rajasthan HC administration issued an amended roster for the period, assigning PIL matters to court no. 3, comprising Justice Inderjeet Singh and Justice Sandeep Taneja.The move came as two Jodhpur bar associations extended their boycott of Justice Sharma till Sept 6, demanding he be kept away from judicial and administrative duties. Rajasthan HC Lawyers’ Association and Rajasthan HC Advocates’ Association of Jodhpur resolved to abstain from court appearances.The bars had decided to submit a memorandum to the President, PM, CJI Surya Kant and senior Collegium judges, seeking a permanent full-time CJ for Rajasthan HC and an immediate end to the “targeted file system” across the state.The confrontation followed three letters Justice Sandeep Mehta wrote to the CJI on Aug 2, 10 and 17, seeking Justice Sharma’s transfer out of Rajasthan.Mehta accused Justice Sharma of misusing administrative powers and interfering in case listing, and sought a CJ from another state.In Jaipur, lawyers gathered outside Justice Sharma’s courtroom, shouted slogans and staged a brief sit-in Monday. Addressing an open court after lawyers blocked appearances before his bench, the acting CJ said: “The situation is a little tense today, as the lawyers are not allowing anyone to appear before the court.”Jodhpur bars appealed to lawyers across Rajasthan to join the movement.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal of Chhattisgarh HC as Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC. The Collegium also recommended Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as CJ of J&K HC. Hours before the recommendation, Sharma decided to abstain from judicial work from Sept 1 to 5.

Article Title: ABVP pulls off a rare repeat in Panjab University polls: Retains president post, 1st back-to-back win since 2014
Article Text:
Chandigarh, Aug 31 (ANI): Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and SOI (Student Organisation of India) members celebrate after ABVP candidate Ankit Bidhan won the Punjab University Student Council election, in Chandigarh on Monday. (ANI Video Grab)

Retains PUCSC Prez Post, First Back-to-Back Wins Since ’14





CHANDIGARH: After ending its 48-year wait for the PUCSC presidency last year, ABVP retained the post on Monday, becoming the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small.ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,149 this year. Yet that solitary vote marks the difference between a historic breakthrough and an equally historic repeat.The total presidential vote was almost identical too. Last year, the eight candidates and NOTA together polled 9,613 votes; this year, the four candidates and NOTA accounted for 9,610. The size of the presidential vote pool barely changed- but its distribution did.In 2025, Sohal’s 3,148 votes were followed by Student Front’s Sumit Kumar at 2,660, NSUI’s Parabjot Singh Gill at 1,359 and ASAP’s Mankirat Mann at 1,184. This year, Ankit’s 3,149 was followed by ASAP’s Aadil Brar at 2,637, NSUI’s Gurman Singh Sidhu at 2,263 and SATH’s Darshpreet Singh at 1,387. NOTA fell from 188 to 174.The change in the field matters. Sohal had won 32.75 per cent of the presidential vote last year; Ankit’s share is almost identical at 32.8 per cent.Yet the winning margin increased from 488 to 512 votes. ABVP’s vote base has effectively remained unchanged while its lead has grown.That points to the opposition arithmetic. Last year, Sumit alone came within 488 votes of Sohal, while Gill and Mann together polled 2,543. This year, the opposition vote was still larger collectively, but it was divided among three challengers, with none matching Sumit’s 2,660.For ABVP, there was another significant change. Last year, the organisation itself was divided, with the ABVP Front contesting the vice-president’s post separately; its candidate Naveen Kumar polled 2,828. This year, the outfit went to the polls together.
Article Summary: ABVP becomes the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small. ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,.149 this year.

Article Title: First exam reforms, now 'school thik karo' campaign: How CJP is changing the discourse of politics
Article Text:
School students protest in UP

'Ministers’ dogs got better facilities than students'

CJP claims credit

Political parties take a cue from CJP

Youth outreach

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the biggest issue facing government school students today? Lack of teachers Poor infrastructure Caste discrimination Inadequate facilities 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: From colleges to schools. From Gen Z to Gen Alpha. From Jantar Mantar to cities and villages in states. The students’ protest has continued; only the stage has shifted. The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo” campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks. Gen Alpha took the cue and brought the protests to villages and towns across states, demanding better school infrastructure and government accountability.The CJP campaign asking for school audits in villages got a huge response. The pictures and videos of schools uploaded on CJP’s X timeline exposed the sorry state of government schools across states. This was followed by ground inspections by CJP teams, which led to confrontation and a strong pushback by some state governments.Two days after the CJP launched its campaign and announced that schools in Rajasthan would be on its radar, the state education department issued new guidelines regulating the entry of outsiders, including media personnel, into government schools.Under the directives, photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live streaming involving students or school activities on campus needed prior permission from the school principal or head of the institution.The Rajasthan order went on to threaten action under applicable laws in case of any breach.So, when a CJP team went to inspect a government school on August 21, it was attacked and forcibly pushed back, allegedly by the locals. Videos of the incident showed a large number of people engaging in a heated exchange with the CJP team, pushing and shoving its members as they tried to enter the village. Some clips also showed stone-pelting and smashed windows of cars. Locals said the village did not need outside political groups to intervene in the school’s affairs.This perhaps became the July 20 Jantar Mantar moment (when Delhi Police used force to stop Gen Z protesters from their Sansad march) of the CJP school campaign as the violent confrontation propelled the issue to the national centre stage.Meanwhile in Uttar Pradesh, Gen Alpha students of a government school staged a protest twice, in a span of four days. over shortage of subject teachers. They briefly blocked traffic also. Students of a government school in Kannauj boycotted classes and held protests against the principal for alleged caste discrimination and ordering the felling of trees inside the school campus. The students of PM Shri Composite School in Gugarapur surrounded the vehicle of the in-charge principal at the school gate as he was leaving and raised slogans against him.Protests also happened in Fatehpur, Hamirpur against lack of facilities in schools. In Hamirpur, 'Gen Alpha' children laid siege to the collectorate to demand the construction of a paved road to their school.In Unnao, hundreds of students of a government-run residential school staged a protest over alleged poor-quality food, inadequate drinking water, shortage of teachers and the behaviour of the principal, briefly disrupting traffic at a city crossing.In Maharashtra, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke conducted a social audit of government-run and municipal schools in Latur district. He led a team at a Zilla Parishad school at Ujani village in Latur's Ausa tehsil.After his audit, Dipke said schools in the state were in a pitiable condition, and even "ministers’ dogs got better facilities" than students. He sought the resignation of Maharashtra school education minister Dada Bhuse. Later, Maharashtra police registered a case against the CJP convenor and others for allegedly entering a government school without permission, disrupting official work and threatening teachers.The state governments cited rules to browbeat the CJP teams away from its schools. But at the same time, they were forced to act to nullify the impact of the CJP campaign. So, while some states announced new measures to improve the condition of schools, others increased the pace of work already underway to ensure that results were seen on the ground quickly.The CJP was quick to claim credit for govt actions and basked in glory.“The impact we’ve been able to make with such a small team in such a short span of time is just unreal. Multiple state governments have had to bow down. Authorities had to listen to Gen Z and Gen Alpha kids and give them their due,” it said in a post on X.“But this does not end here. We need to keep going until even the remotest regions of the nation, even the most deprived communities, have access to the highest standard of educational facilities. They may use force, they may file cases, they may do whatever they can to crush this, but we will remain committed to the same demand,” the post read.While it can be debated whether or not the CJP campaign forced the governments into action, what can be said with certainty is that the CJP has managed to do what many political parties could not - inspire the youth to come to the streets and seek accountability from power.The two CJP campaigns also point to an interesting shift - which should be a learning lesson, especially for parties in the opposition space. We have seen the opposition parties raise the pitch against government on issues like caste and religion as these have greater potential for voter mobilisation. Rarely do we see campaigns by the opposition parties centred around health or education reforms. But that seems to have changed.The Congress has taken a cue and is trying to stay focused on students’ connect and raise issues that concern the youth. In Rajasthan, the state Congress unit is also on the streets to highlight gaps in state government school infrastructure.And it’s not just the opposition that is course-correcting; the ruling BJP has also drawn a roadmap to engage with the youth and understand their concerns. In the middle of the Gen Z protest, Prime Minister Narendra Modi debuted on Instagram and tried to communicate directly with the youth who were on the streets. The BJP has in fact formed a dedicated team to spearhead its Gen Z outreach. The team includes BJP chief Nitin Nabin, national general secretaries Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde, Gujarat minister Harsh Sanghavi, Chhattisgarh minister OP Choudhary, along with several other leaders.Clearly, the CJP has managed to change the political discourse and has put the focus on the youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics. As we gear up for the next rounds of assembly elections in the run-up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge, we may see youth outreach taking centre stage like never before.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo’ campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks.

Article Title: In 1978, Richard Branson bought a bare 74-acre Caribbean island for $180,000; it now shelters more than 140 animal species, including breeding lemurs and giant tortoises
Article Text:
An aerial view of Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands, a private island in the Caribbean. Credits - Wikimedia Commons

A reluctant purchase becomes a passion

Building a home for species with nowhere else to go

The Great House on Necker Island, built after Hurricane Irene. Credits - Wikipedia

A sanctuary that sustains itself

In 1978, Richard Branson, then 28, paid $180,000 for a small, uninhabited island in the British Virgin Islands. Necker Island had no fresh water source, no buildings and barely any vegetation beyond scrub and cactus. Nearly fifty years after the purchase, and roughly four decades since the resort itself was completed, that same 74-acre island supports a working conservation programme that shelters well over 140 species, several of which now breed there naturally, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles.Branson has told the story of the purchase many times over the years, and the details rarely change. According to an account he has given describing the negotiation, he first visited the British Virgin Islands on a trip meant to impress a woman he was pursuing at the time, having been offered a free look at the islands by a realtor who did not realise how little money Branson actually had. The asking price for Necker was around six million dollars, far beyond what he could afford at the time, running an eight-year-old record label, so Branson made an opening offer of just $100,000.The seller turned him down at first but came back a year later, still unable to find a buyer, and eventually accepted a revised offer of $180,000. At that point he owned essentially raw land, with no infrastructure, and the sale came with a condition that he build a resort on the site within four years. Turning that bare ground into something worth visiting took nearly a decade and set the pattern for what followed: a slow, deliberate transformation rather than a quick development.The wildlife did not arrive all at once, and it was introduced deliberately. Over the decades since the resort was completed, Branson and his team have deliberately introduced species that were struggling in their native ranges, choosing Necker specifically because its isolation from the mainland makes it easier to protect animals from predators and disease, even though the island itself operates as a small, tightly controlled private resort where guest access to the animals is limited and managed by the conservation team. As Branson explains in a PBS documentary filmed on the island, lemurs have become one of what he calls the island's flagship conservation species, brought in after habitat loss in Madagascar left many of their relatives fighting for survival at home. Giant tortoises, native to the Aldabra atoll in the Seychelles, followed a similar path, arriving as part of a breeding programme rather than as a decorative addition to the grounds. Flamingos, macaws, iguanas and a rotating cast of other species have joined them, each one added with the specific aim of giving vulnerable animals a secure place to establish new populations. That patient approach appears to be paying off in the way conservationists actually measure success, through births rather than just headcounts.Today, the tortoises in particular have reached a milestone that is rare in captive conservation work, breeding naturally on the island rather than relying on animals shipped in from elsewhere to maintain their numbers. The breeding success became especially significant in 2021, when the island recorded its first Aldabra giant tortoise hatchlings. The young animals were discovered soon after emerging from their nests and were monitored by the island's conservation team to make sure they remained healthy. The event showed that the tortoises were not simply surviving in an introduced population but were completing an important part of their life cycle on Necker itself. The island's wildlife programme has followed a similar approach with other species, creating conditions in which animals can establish themselves rather than simply being displayed for visitors. Virgin Limited Edition now describes Necker as a natural breeding ground for several rare species, including Madagascan lemurs, giant tortoises, rock lizards and flamingos.A dedicated wildlife team now manages the island's animal population full time, treating Necker less like a private garden and more like a functioning sanctuary with its own breeding programmes and veterinary oversight. Branson himself has framed it in exactly those terms in his own public comments, describing a personal commitment to protecting disappearing species that has clearly outlasted his initial reasons for buying the place at all. Necker Island remains one of a small number of personal purchases from that era that developed decades later into an active conservation programme.
Article Summary: Richard Branson bought Necker Island in 1978 for just $180,000. The 74-acre island now supports a working conservation programme. It shelters well over 140 species, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles. A dedicated wildlife team manages the island's population full time.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Agassi’s famous quote, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children's childhood,” offers a look at how becoming a parent changed his view of his own life. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood.

Article Title: Alaska used rotenone to eliminate invasive pike from an entire lake; the pike vanished, and 6,836 Arctic char were later stocked to rebuild the native fishery
Article Text:
Representative image

Why northern pike are a problem in Alaska

Rotenone: a targeted, temporary reset

Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char

Stormy Lake: a case study in eradication and recovery

Other lakes, similar stories

Why Arctic char matter

Balancing restoration with public concern

A tool, not a silver bullet

In a remote corner of Southcentral Alaska, state biologists carried out a dramatic restoration: they treated an entire lake with rotenone, a plant-derived piscicide, to wipe out an invasive population of northern pike. After the treatment, post-surveys confirmed the pike were gone. The next step was rebuilding what had been lost. In June 2013, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into the now pike-free lake, jump-starting the recovery of a native fishery that had been pushed out by the predator. This account draws on ADF&G’s technical reports and project summaries documenting the rotenone treatment and restocking. Read on to know more:Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century and have since spread through connected waterways, especially as warming temperatures and changing hydrology make it easier for them to move and survive. As apex predators, pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. In some lakes, they have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities and altering food webs.ADF&G describes pike as a major threat to endemic fish populations and has pursued a mix of suppression and eradication strategies depending on the waterbody. In isolated lakes where pike can be completely removed, the agency has turned to rotenone as the most practical and efficient tool.Rotenone is a naturally occurring compound derived from certain tropical plants. It has been used for decades in fisheries management to remove unwanted fish from lakes and streams. When applied at carefully calculated concentrations, it blocks oxygen uptake in fish gills, killing fish while leaving most other aquatic organisms unaffected. The chemical breaks down relatively quickly in sunlight and warm water; in many Alaskan projects, detectable levels drop to near zero within weeks to months.There are only two proven methods to eradicate invasive fish from lakes: completely draining the waterbody or using a piscicide like rotenone. For most lakes, draining is not feasible, making rotenone the default option for full eradication. Before treatment, ADF&G typically relocates any desirable native fish, such as salmon or trout, to safe holding areas or other lakes, then treats the target lake and its outlet streams to ensure no pike survive.Stormy Lake, near Anchorage, is one of the clearest examples of this approach. In fall 2012, ADF&G treated Stormy Lake and its outlet creek with liquid rotenone to eradicate an established northern pike population. Post-treatment evaluations—including netting and electrofishing surveys, found no surviving pike, confirming the treatment’s success.Once the rotenone had fully degraded (by late January 2013, about four months after application), the agency began restocking. Native fish that had been held in offsite net pens were reintroduced in March 2013, and on June 17, 2013, ADF&G stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into Stormy Lake. These char were of mixed Stormy Lake and Dolly Varden Lake parentage, helping to re-establish a robust, genetically diverse population.The project’s final report, published in ADF&G’s Sport Fish Research series, describes the effort as a successful model for eradicating invasive pike and restoring native fisheries.Stormy Lake is not unique. ADF&G has used rotenone to remove pike from multiple lakes in the Anchorage and Mat-Su areas, including Sand Lake, Anderson Lake and Kings Lake. In each case, the sequence is similar: treat the lake, confirm pike are gone, then restock with native species such as rainbow trout, Arctic char and grayling.For example, after rotenone treatments in 2020, Anderson and Kings lakes were declared pike-free and added to the Northern Cook Inlet stocking program in 2021. Both lakes were restocked with rainbow trout, restoring sport fisheries that had been lost to pike predation. In Anchorage, pike have been eradicated from all but one of five lakes where they were confirmed, with Lower Fire Lake remaining a management challenge.Arctic char are a prized native species in Alaska, valued both ecologically and by anglers. They thrive in cold, clear lakes and are an important part of the natural food web. In lakes where pike have been removed, char are often a key restocking target because they can grow to good size, support recreational fishing and help re-establish a more natural predator–prey balance.In Stormy Lake, the 6,836 char stocked in 2013 were intended to re-create a self-sustaining population that could eventually support a catch-and-release or limited-harvest fishery. Monitoring in subsequent years showed that char, along with other restocked natives, were surviving and growing, indicating the lake was returning to a healthier, pre-pike state.The use of rotenone is not without controversy. Killing all fish in a lake, even temporarily, can be unsettling for nearby residents and anglers. ADF&G addresses these concerns through public meetings, environmental assessments and detailed explanations of why the treatment is necessary and how risks are managed.Agency biologists say allowing pike to remain in the lakes can pose a greater threat to native biodiversity and long-term fishing opportunities. In lakes where pike have become established, native fish may not recover without removing the invasive population completely. When used correctly, rotenone can help achieve this reset, allowing fisheries to be rebuilt with native species.While rotenone has proven effective in isolated lakes, it is not a solution for every pike-infested waterbody. In large, connected systems like much of the Mat-Su Valley, complete eradication is currently impossible because pike can simply move back in from untreated areas. There, ADF&G focuses on suppression, using gillnets, targeted rotenone applications in key tributaries, and liberal harvest rules to keep pike numbers down in priority fisheries.Projects like Stormy Lake show where eradication is still feasible: in relatively closed basins where pike can be fully removed and native fish reintroduced. For those lakes, the combination of rotenone treatment and strategic stocking—like the 6,836 Arctic char released in 2013, offers a path back to a more natural, resilient fishery. For Alaska’s fisheries managers, such projects demonstrate that invasive predators can sometimes be removed and native fish populations rebuilt when the conditions are right. Article Summary: Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century. Pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. They have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Apple’s CEO John Ternus: “Build what interests you, build what excites you, but above all…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by John Ternus

“Build what interests you,

build what excites you

, but above all else, build it in a way that aligns with your values.”

What John Ternus meant by building around your values

Ternus built his career on the engineering side of Apple

Ternus's work went far beyond how an Apple device looked

Ternus became Apple CEO in 2026

Ternus's three-part test adds a missing question to career advice

Building does not mean getting everything right

Lessons to learn from John Ternus’s quote

Let curiosity guide your direction

Choose something that keeps you engaged

Do not follow passion blindly

Keep your values involved in your decisions

Think beyond the finished result

Know what is worth your effort

Balance ambition with principles

Build something you can stand behind

John Ternus has spent much of his career working behind products that people use every day, dealing with the engineering decisions that determine how those products look, work and hold up over time. Now, as Apple’s chief executive, his words about building have a wider audience. In a 2024 commencement address at the University of Pennsylvania, Ternus told graduates to build things that interest and excite them, while making sure those things fit their values. The advice is straightforward, but the final part changes its meaning. It is not simply about finding enjoyable work or chasing an interesting idea. It asks people to think about what they are creating and whether it reflects the principles they want to stand behind. Coming from an engineer whose career has centred on designing and developing hardware, the choice of the word 'build' is particularly fitting.The quote was delivered by Ternus during his 2024 commencement speech at the University of Pennsylvania, where he had studied mechanical engineering. The first part of Ternus’s advice is about curiosity. People tend to spend a great deal of their working lives on a relatively small number of subjects, so having a genuine interest in the problem can make a difference.Excitement adds something slightly different. Being interested in a subject does not necessarily mean finding every part of the work enjoyable. Difficult projects can involve repetition, setbacks and long stretches when progress is hard to see. Ternus’s point is not that work should always be fun. It is that there should be something about the work that keeps a person engaged with it.Then comes the qualification: values come first. That shifts the quote away from simple career advice. A project can be technically impressive or personally exciting and still not be something a person wants to help create. Values provide the boundary around the other two ideas.Ternus’s own professional background makes the language of building especially appropriate.He studied mechanical engineering at the University of Pennsylvania before beginning his career at Virtual Research Systems. He joined Apple in 2001, initially working within the company’s product design organisation. Over the years, his responsibilities expanded across hardware engineering and some of Apple’s most recognisable products.Apple says Ternus became vice president of Hardware Engineering in 2013 and joined the company’s executive team in 2021. His rise was therefore closely tied to the technical side of the company rather than following a conventional route through finance or sales.Ternus eventually became senior vice president of Hardware Engineering, overseeing the teams responsible for Apple’s hardware development.That role placed him close to the practical process of turning ideas into finished products. Hardware engineering involves far more than the appearance of a device. Materials, reliability, manufacturing, durability and the interaction between different components all have to work together.The position also meant working across several product categories at once. A decision that makes sense for one device may not necessarily work for another. Engineering teams have to balance performance, size, cost, manufacturing constraints and the experience of the person using the finished product.Apple announced in April 2026 that Cook would become executive chairman and Ternus would become CEO on September 1, 2026. His appointment followed years of increasing responsibility within the company.He therefore took over after more than two decades at Apple, much of that time spent working on hardware.The transition also meant that an engineer with extensive experience in product development moved into the role responsible for the company as a whole.Ternus’s quote can be read as a simple three-question test.First, does the subject genuinely interest you?Second, is there something about the work that excites you enough to keep learning and improving?Third, does what you are building fit with your values?The third question is the one that prevents the advice from becoming another version of “follow your passion”.Interest can tell someone where to look. Excitement can help sustain attention. Values can help determine where the line should be drawn.There is also an important implication in the word “build”.A finished product is usually the visible result of many versions that never reached the public. Ideas are tested, changed, rejected and rebuilt. The same can happen with a career.Ternus’s own path at Apple was not a single leap from engineer to chief executive. He moved through different positions and took on broader responsibilities over many years.That makes the quote less about finding one perfect project and more about deciding what is worth continuing to work on. Sometimes the first version is wrong. That does not necessarily mean the entire idea has failed. It may simply need to be rebuilt.
Article Summary: John Ternus gave the quote at the University of Pennsylvania in 2024. He has spent much of his career working on the hardware side of Apple. The advice is straightforward, but the final part changes its meaning. It asks people to think about what they are creating and whether it reflects principles they want to stand behind.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam

RCB register their second win

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) beat Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Theatre review: The dawn that never comes
Article Text:
A still from Wo Subah Hum Hi Se Aayegi​

Wo Subah Hum Hi Se Aayegi

ladka

ladki

Chhaya Geet

Wo Subah Hum Hi Se Aayegi

Want us to review your play? Mail us at tims.delhitimes@timesofindia.com





begins with a lot of promise. It suggests that it will be a revolutionary, passionate tale of youth rising to the challenge, that it will address the transformation of both the self and the state, and how the two are often correlated.However, ten minutes into the Mahesh Bhatt play, you realise that it is instead reminiscent of a ’90s Bollywood film, where a hard-workingcrosses paths with an effervescent, and they end up falling for each other.Much like a Hindi movie, there are also the usual bygone tropes that were once a hit formula – a drunk father, a dead mother, sad music, a second, more successful male lead, and a chirpy younger brother.The stage looked bright and was well set, while the actors did what they were told. Playwright Dinesh Gautam had some interesting ideas too, but they were never fully developed.For instance, the meta-interview structure with which the play begins, when the audience is first introduced to Ajay – a UPSC aspirant from Bihar – is abandoned for the rest of the play before eventually returning to close the story.Perhaps the strongest socio-political material arrives relatively late, particularly in the discussion around reservation and caste, but it too never matures.However, not all is lost to the whims and fancies of a melodramatic cliché. There are a few isolated good moments, including the nostalgic touch of Vividh Bharti and its programme,The handful of comic lines that do land belong to the waiter. And the drunk dad is realistic enough to immerse you in the world of Kavita, Ajay and their predictable romance.Unfortunately, it still can’t save the largely underwhelming writing.To round off the unsurprising turn of events,ends on a note where Kavita’s apparent rejection of Ajay is revealed to be a lie.Therefore, the play’s most interesting – and perhaps most innovative – theatrical device, the interview format, is also ultimately sacrificed at the altar of an expected filmy happy ending.-Anvita Singh
Article Summary: Mahesh Bhatt's Wo Subah Hum Hi Se Aayegi is reminiscent of a ’90s Bollywood film. There are also the usual bygone tropes that were once a hit formula. The strongest socio-political material arrives relatively late, particularly in the discussion around reservation and caste.

Article Title: Bus rape: Fingerprints confirm accused’s presence; CCTV not working, say cops
Article Text:
Inquiries have revealed that the conductor talked to the girl for 5-7 minutes after she sought a lift at Pari Chowk in Noida on Aug 4.

CCTV on bus not functional at time of incident, say cops





NEW DELHI: DNA evidence will be key against the two accused in the gang rape of a 17-year-old in a moving sleeper bus on Aug 4, police said.Fingerprints of the survivor and the accused — driver Kuldeep and conductor Sandeep — have confirmed their presence in the bus; samples have also been picked up from the seats and steering wheel, sleuths said.Clothes worn by the accused have also been seized and sent for examination.A detailed forensic report is awaited, sources said. A special team has been formed to investigate the case.Inquiries have revealed that the conductor talked to the girl for 5-7 minutes after she sought a lift at Pari Chowk in Noida on Aug 4.After he learnt she had left home follow­ing a fight and was headed to her cousin’s in Noida’s Sector 63, Sandeep told her the bus was headed that way. Soon aft­er she boarded the bus, Sandeep raped her at Bakhtawarpur Village (Noida Sec 127-128), police said. Then, the conductor took the wheel and the driver forced himself on the girl.After the assault, the bus travelled 26km unchecked before the duo dropped the girl at Kashmere Gate bus stand.Police said thick curtains were installed on the bus windows, blocking off any view from outside.The girl reported the crime to Kashmere Gate police.Following the incident, Delhi Traffic Police is checking buses at the interstate bus terminals, verifying dri­v­ers’ IDs and other documents.Both accused were arrested from Timarpur, around 5km from Kashmere Gate, within hours of the crime and the bus seized. A blanket was found placed over the steering wheel near the driver’s seat, while a bedsheet had been spread across the empty aisle between the seats on either side. This was where the alleged assault took place, police said.Kuldeep and Sandeep had been working with the bus company for the past two years. Police found at least 11 traffic challans amounting to Rs 54,000 pending against the bus at the time of the incident.Police have collected CCTV footage from places on the bus’s route, starting from where it was parked in Surajpur, Noida, for repairs, to where the girl was dropped off. Statements of the employees at the workshop have confirmed that the accused driver and conductor were present there and had taken the bus out after work was completed, police said.The digital video recorder of the bus has also been examined but cops found that the bus’ CCTV was not functional at the time. The device is being examined to ascertain the last recording time and whether the accused turned it off before the incident. An employee of the bus company told cops that the bus had gone for repairs and was being renovated so the CCTV cameras had not been installed. After Surajpur, the bus was supposed to head to Kashmere Gate for painting work.
Article Summary: Fingerprints of the survivor and the accused — driver Kuldeep and conductor Sandeep — have confirmed their presence in the bus. DNA samples have also been picked up from the seats and steering wheel, sleuths said. A detailed forensic report is awaited, sources said.

Article Title: 3 months on, family that lost 8 struggles to cope
Article Text:
New Delhi:

TOI





“We have still not been able to move on,” a relative of the Aggarwal family, eight of whose members were killed in the Hauz Rani B&B blaze on June 3, toldTuesday.The eight had gathered at the B&B to meet family patriarch Radheshyam Aggarwal (76), who was undergoing treatment for an acute lung infection at a nearby private hospital in Saket. What was supposed to be a reunion ended in a tragedy that wiped out an entire branch of the family.Among those killed were Radheshyam’s wife Premlata (70), son Vivek (47), daughter-in-law Tarjani (42), and granddaughters Jivisha (20) and Varya (16). Three relatives of Premlata who had travelled from Kishangarh in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district — Kamla (52), Ashok (56) and Jhaveri — also died in the blaze.The tragedy was compounded by Radheshyam’s death soon after. In his final days, as he waited to see his family, relatives shielded him from the devastating truth, telling him that his son was away on work to Jaipur.The relatives and cousins of the eight are now left to cope with the loss. In the days after the tragedy, they had demanded strict punishment for those operating the B&B without necessary permissions.The Aggarwals lived as a joint family in south Delhi’s Kotla Mubarakpur until a few years ago, when they moved to Gurgaon.Premlata, Vivek, Tarjani and Varya, fondly called Pearl, had travelled from their home in Gurgaon. Jivisha, known to the family as Angel, flew in from Bengaluru just hours before the blaze.Kamla, Ashok and Jhaveri initially planned to leave earlier but extended their stay at the family’s insistence — a decision that would leave their loved ones confronting an unbearable loss.For the entire family, the filing of the chargesheet marks another chapter in a tragedy they are still struggling to process, three months after the fire took away eight of their own.
Article Summary: Eight members of the Aggarwal family were killed in the Hauz Rani B&B blaze on June 3. The eight had gathered at the B &B to meet family patriarch Radheshyam AggarWal (76) who was undergoing treatment for an acute lung infection at a nearby private hospital.

Article Title: Crowds, funds and competition: Why Mumbai’s Ganpati idols keep getting taller
Article Text:
Despite the growing scale of idols, there is no government-prescribed cap on their height.

‘Race of taller idols driven by competition to lure crowds’





MUMBAI: In 2022, Malvani Mhada Cha Raja stood around 22-ft tall. The next year, it grew to 28 ft. Then came 32-33 ft. Last year, the idol towered 36 ft above visitors. The steady climb has not been by accident.“This is nothing but a competition. If one mandal brings an idol, another wants to bring the same or something bigger,” said Mustakim Sayyed, a founding member of the mandal, adding internal politics within mandals also drives the trend.Two people were killed and five injured when a 22-ft-tall idol collapsed during an arrival procession in Bhuleshwar on Aug 22. The accident has cast a spotlight on a competition of heights that has transformed Ganeshotsav, reports Abhishek Singh.Mumbai’s giant-idol culture is often traced to Ganesh Galli in Lalbaug, where the Lalbaug Sarvajanik Utsav Ma­ndal introduced a 22-ft Ganpati in 1977 during its golden jubilee. The bar kept rising: Khetwadi’s 12th Lane installed a 40-ft idol in 2000, while Khetwadi’s 11th Lane produced a 45-ft idol in 2023 and is set to take it to 47 ft this year.While the competition can become a show of st­rength, it’s also driven by a desire to lure cr­owds.Bigger idols also mean bigger investments. A 10-15-ft idol can start at around Rs 3.5 lakh, while a 40-45-ft idol can cost Rs 12-13 lakh, according to sculptor Siddhesh Dighole.Nikhil Morye of Brihanmumbai Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Samanvay Samiti attributes the competition to the human instinct to outdo one another. Murtikar Rajan Zard said the pressure from mandals is unmistakable.“There is always a competition between mandals; they want their Ganpati to be bigger than the one in the neighbouring mandal. They may not say it directly, but we understand what they want.”Zard believes idols up to 15 ft are safest and those up to 20 ft can be managed with adequate support. But commercial pressure remains. “If we don’t do something new, the advertising money won’t come. And if the advertisements don’t come, mandals cannot afford to conduct the festival.”For Umesh Sitaram Naik, former chairman and current Karyakarini Sadasya of 107-year-old Chinchpokli Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal, problem lies in what happens when increasingly large idols have to be moved. “A 40-foot idol may not be a problem if it remains in one place, but when you have to move it, transport it and finally immerse it, the risks are very different. The sculptor also needs the experience and expertise to build an idol of that height safely,” he said.Despite the growing scale of idols, there is no government-prescribed cap on their height. Prashant Sapkale, BMC deputy municipal commissioner for zone II, said the issue had not been discussed in recent years. Nor is there a BMC team that certifies the structural stability or safety of idols.“There is no such team from BMC that works on the structural stability or safety of the idols...There is no standard engineering method or formula being used to guarantee stability. Generally, the sculptors themselves ensure it,” Sapkale said, adding that the Bhuleshwar incident had led to greater caution during transportation.This is not the first time giant idols have come under the glare. After the collapse of a 22-ft idol before immersion in 2011, the Salgaonkar committee proposed an 18-foot limit in 2012, but it did not endure.During Covid, public mandal idols were capped at four feet in 2020 and 2021; the restrictions were later lifted.Sociologist Dipti Shahu said the competition can become a show of strength. “An idol attracting lakhs of people becomes a matter of pride for the mandal, creating a hype that can turn into a show of strength: ‘I can do better than you.’” But the competition is also driven by crowds.In the suburbs, mandals increasingly want to offer devotees an experience comparable to visiting popular idols in South Mumbai, said Sameer Bambardekar, 50, a member of Upnagar Cha Raja Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal in Borivli.His mandal increased its idol from eight feet to 25 ft in 2006 to mark its 25th anniversary. Soon, several mandals in Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar and Bhayander also began installing larger idols. “Why would someone go to South Mumbai and queue up for six to eight hours if they could see idols of the same height on this side in just one hour?” he said.And where crowds go, advertising follows. With around 2,500-3,000 pandals registered in the city every year, they are competing for a limited pool of sponsors. “An advertiser will ask, ‘If I invest Rs 50,000 with your mandal, what benefit will I get? If I put up a stall here, how many people are going to visit it?’ So, footfall has become an important factor in the competition,” Morye said.“The bigger the idol, the more material and work it requires. But mandals cannot assume that sponsorship will rise in proportion to the idol’s height. Sponsors look at the mandal’s reach, location and footfall. For a sculptor, making a very large idol also means investing heavily in new moulds. That is why I make idols only up to 24-25 ft; there are very few mandals willing to pay Rs 7-8 lakh or more,” he added.For engineer-turned-farmer Rajesh Gadepatil, 56, the race has become a display of power and prestige. “A mentality of ‘the taller it is, the greater it is; the grander it is, the superior it is’ has taken root. As the crowds increase, power, publicity, politics and money also find their way into the festival. We need to ask ourselves whether, in the name of Ganeshotsav, we are trying to make Ganesha greater, society greater, or simply our own mandal greater?”
Article Summary: Two people were killed and five injured when a 22-ft-tall idol collapsed during an arrival procession in Bhuleshwar on Aug 22. The accident has cast a spotlight on a competition of heights that has transformed Ganeshotsav. There is no government-prescribed cap on their height.
